hook: This is the farthest you can get from the sea.

beats.narration: This is the farthest you can get from the sea.
It's in Xinjiang, in north-western China, near the borders with Kazakhstan and Mongolia.
beats.claim: The Eurasian pole of inaccessibility is in Xinjiang, north-western China.

beats.narration: Draw a circle around it with a radius of two and a half thousand kilometres, and you still don't touch the ocean.
beats.claim: The two candidate points are about 2,510 and 2,514 km from the sea.

beats.narration: That's roughly London to Moscow, with nothing but land.
beats.claim: London (51.51N, 0.13W) to Moscow (55.76N, 37.62E) great-circle distance is about 2,500 km.

beats.narration: The old answer said two thousand six hundred and forty five kilometres. Then researchers counted the Gulf of Ob, a Siberian inlet that reaches about a thousand kilometres inland.
beats.claim: Older figure 2,645 km; the 2007 revision accounted for the Gulf of Ob, which reaches about 1,000 km inland.

beats.narration: Now there are two points, almost tied, within the margin of error.
beats.claim: EPIA1 ~2,510 km and EPIA2 ~2,514 km from the ocean, margins ±10 and ±7 km.

beats.narration: Want the beach from here? Pack a lunch. Pack several.

title: The farthest you can get from the sea
description: The Eurasian pole of inaccessibility, in Xinjiang, China: about 2,510 km from the nearest ocean.
